thread:
Priya: heads up — customer running Private (on-prem) asked for a security checklist. primary asks: 1) KMS integration with customer HSM (no outbound to our KMS), 2) RBAC changes during maintenance windows, 3) audit log retention + immutable store, 4) network policy lockdown, 5) vuln triage/incident steps. any quick notes before i reply?

Leo: +1. for HSM we should support a customer-managed KMS endpoint (bring-your-own-key) and document a local PKCS#11 path. ask: do they want in-cluster key agents or sidecar access?

Marta: prefer agent that talks to HSM over mTLS to minimize node-level secrets. vendor HSMs usually provide a network endpoint we can route inside VPC. note: document must call out offline rotation process.

Sam: on RBAC: we should recommend a deny-by-default K8s RBAC baseline and scoped service accounts for all runtime components. during maintenance, use time-limited escalation via OIDC session tokens, not changing clusterroles permanently. for automation: terraform + vault-issued short-lived creds.

Priya: good. audit logs — customer needs immutability for compliance. recommended flow: audit -> local append-only log -> forward to S3/GCS with bucket lock + SSE-KMS using customer CMK. retention policy should be configurable per-tenant.

Marta: add checksum + periodic integrity scans (sha256) for log files. also ship to third-party SIEM optionally.

Leo: network policies: default deny inbound/outbound at namespace level, allow only these egress targets: (1) HSM ip range, (2) customer private registry, (3) NTP, (4) internal metrics/logging endpoints. no direct internet egress from inference pods.

Sam: example NetworkPolicy snippet for egress whitelist:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-except-approved
  namespace: redwood-runtime
spec:
  podSelector: {} # applies to all pods in ns
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.40.0.0/16 # HSM range (example)
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.41.0.0/16 # registry
    - to:
      - podSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: internal-logging
    ports:
    - protocol: UDP
      port: 123 # NTP
```

Priya: nice. also require egress DNS resolution to an internal resolver only. don't allow pods to talk to 8.8.8.8.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: runbook_exists=true rbac_baseline=deny-by-default kms_integration=customer-managed_hsm audit_forwarding=s3_immutable_network_policies=ns-default-deny

Sam: vuln triage: if runtime CVE found in container base image -> immediate mitigation: patch build with minimal diff, create canary rollout to dedicated pool, monitor latency/regressions, then full rollout. if kernel escape suspected -> cordon node, isolate, collect memory + dmesg, escalate to infra oncall, rotate node credentials, recreate nodes.

Marta: incident response for KMS compromise scenario: revoke any derived tokens, rotate data keys, issue new CMK on customer HSM if supported, and run integrity checks on model weights (checksums). document communication timeline for customers.

Priya: we need a short customer-facing checklist and an internal runbook. i'll draft both. things to include: RBAC baseline commands (kubectl examples), NetworkPolicy templates, KMS connector config example, audit-forwarding terraform snippet, incident playbooks.

Leo: small nit — include a pre-check script to validate no hostNetwork: true on inference pods and that capability additions (SYS_ADMIN) are blocked in pod security policy/admission.

Sam: also validate iptables on nodes to ensure no accidental wide-open egress created by CNI. include `iptables -L -n` check in preflight.

Priya: ok i'll assemble and post a draft in #eng-security in ~2 hrs. if anyone wants to pair on the KMS connector config ping me. :thumbsup:

sec-bot: note: filed SEC-2026-033 — onprem-kms-integration-reqs, assigned to Priya, SLA: 5d

Marta: thanks — i'll review the draft and add the integrity scan steps.

Leo: happy to sanity-check the RBAC snippets.

Priya: thanks team!
